targetText: Equalisation of the General Rate of Profit Through Competition.
explanation: The rate of profit ($p/C$) measures surplus value relative to total invested capital (constant plus variable), whereas the rate of surplus value ($s/v$) measures exploitation relative to labor costs alone.

targetText: Now, if the commodities are sold at their values, then, as we have shown, very different rates of profit arise in the various spheres of production, depending on the different organic composition of the masses of capital invested in them.
explanation: The organic composition of capital ($c/v$) reflects the ratio of dead labor (machinery and materials) to living labor-power employed in production.

targetText: Between the spheres more or less approximating the average there is again a tendency toward equalization, seeking the ideal average, i.
explanation: The tendential fall of the rate of profit occurs because technological progress increases constant capital faster than living labor power, shrinking the relative source of surplus value.

targetText: But even in other, less developed, modes of production that which is produced in relatively small quantities as a common product by small-scale, even if numerous, producers, is concentrated in large quantities ; at least in the case of the vital commodities ; in the hands of relatively few merchants.
explanation: Commercial or merchant capital doesn’t create new surplus value directly, but collects a share of total social profit by speeding up the circulation and sale of goods.
